slides.title: Breakthrough fungal infection
paragraphs: Confirm infection and seek species identification, histopathology, and susceptibility testing when feasible. Review adherence, formulation, absorption, interactions, achieved exposure, devices, drainage, immune recovery, and whether a second fungus lies outside the current spectrum. Persistent infection may reflect inadequate source control despite a low MIC. [2]
Fellow teaching
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Breakthrough fungal infection Confirm infection and seek species identification, histopathology, and susceptibility testing when feasible. Review adherence, formulation, absorption, interactions, achieved exposure, devices, drainage, immune recovery, and whether a second fungus lies outside the current spectrum. Persistent infection may reflect inadequate source control despite a low MIC. [2] Fellow teaching MIC interpretation across drug classes Breakpoints depend on organism, method, drug exposure, and available outcomes. An epidemiological cutoff identifies a non-wild-type population; it is not a clinical susceptible breakpoint. For Aspergillus tested against echinocandins, laboratories often assess minimum effective concentration rather than the same MIC endpoint used for azoles. MIC values cannot be compared directly across classes to rank clinical efficacy. [2] Hypoalbuminemia, obesity, critical illness, ECMO, and impaired absorption can complicate interpretation of total plasma levels. Review dosing and level interpretation with pharmacy when these factors are present. [3] Newer experimental posaconazole data show that infection alters cerebral diffusion. These animal data do not establish a human CNS dose or clinical equivalence to voriconazole. [36]

slides.title: Newer approved antifungals
rows: Candidemia and invasive candidiasis with limited or no alternatives. Adult dose 400 mg IV initially, then 200 mg weekly.

Same class gaps and possible FKS cross-resistance. Not studied for Candida endocarditis, osteomyelitis, or meningitis; label safety beyond 4 weekly doses is not established. Infusion reactions, liver effects, and photosensitivity require attention.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Newer approved antifungals Approved indications and limitations Drug / mechanism Established U.S. role Nuance and pitfall Rezafungin / Rezzayo Long-acting echinocandin Candidemia and invasive candidiasis with limited or no alternatives. Adult dose 400 mg IV initially, then 200 mg weekly. Same class gaps and possible FKS cross-resistance. Not studied for Candida endocarditis, osteomyelitis, or meningitis; label safety beyond 4 weekly doses is not established. Infusion reactions, liver effects, and photosensitivity require attention. Ibrexafungerp / Brexafemme Oral triterpenoid glucan-synthase inhibitor Vulvovaginal candidiasis and reduction of recurrent VVC. It is not approved for candidemia step-down. GI effects and CYP3A interactions matter. Pregnancy is contraindicated because of embryo-fetal toxicity. Verify availability separately from approval. Oteseconazole / Vivjoa Tetrazole CYP51 inhibitor Reduction of recurrent VVC in females who are not of reproductive potential. Not a systemic mold or candidemia treatment. Contraindicated in females of reproductive potential, pregnancy, and lactation; prolonged exposure underlies the restriction. Drug interactions still require review. [24] [25] [26]

slides.title: Investigational antifungals
paragraphs: Development status was reviewed October 14, 2026. These agents remain investigational; in vitro activity and sponsor announcements have limited clinical applicability.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Investigational antifungals Development status was reviewed October 14, 2026. These agents remain investigational; in vitro activity and sponsor announcements have limited clinical applicability. Agent Target / route Potential spectrum and gaps Current evidence and status Olorofim Orotomide; inhibits fungal dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking pyrimidine synthesis. Oral development. Aspergillus, including some azole-resistant isolates, and selected difficult molds such as Scedosporium and Lomentospora. No useful Candida or Mucorales coverage. Investigational. OASIS phase 3 topline results were announced in June 2026; the October 6 sponsor statement still says it is unapproved. Full published results and regulatory review are needed to define its role. Fosmanogepix → manogepix Prodrug of a Gwt1 inhibitor affecting GPI-anchored protein maturation; IV and oral development. Broad investigational yeast and mold activity, including many resistant isolates. Important gaps include poor activity against C. krusei and related species; Mucorales activity is inconsistent. Small single-arm phase 2 studies reported clinical activity in candidemia and mold infections; comparative efficacy is not established. Two phase 3 programs for invasive yeast and mold infections were ongoing in the 2026 sponsor update. No established routine clinical TDM target or licensed regimen. Opelconazole Inhaled triazole designed for lung exposure. Local Aspergillus-directed development; inhalation does not establish adequate systemic or CNS therapy. Opera-T phase 3 in refractory pulmonary aspergillosis was terminated January 7, 2026. Sponsor interim analysis reported numerically worse response and higher mortality in the active arm. The unfavorable interim findings limit its proposed clinical role. [27] [28] [29] [30] [31] [32] [33] [34] Fellow teaching New mechanisms and resistance Olorofim is not an azole, and fosmanogepix is not an echinocandin. A new target may retain activity against isolates resistant to older classes. Spectrum, clinical efficacy, and emergence of resistance still require study. Assess the enrolled organisms, comparator, outcomes, follow-up, and safety data before applying trial results. [27] [32]

slides.title: Investigational antifungals
rows: Prodrug of a Gwt1 inhibitor affecting GPI-anchored protein maturation; IV and oral development.
Broad investigational yeast and mold activity, including many resistant isolates. Important gaps include poor activity against C. krusei and related species; Mucorales activity is inconsistent.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Investigational antifungals Development status was reviewed October 14, 2026. These agents remain investigational; in vitro activity and sponsor announcements have limited clinical applicability. Agent Target / route Potential spectrum and gaps Current evidence and status Olorofim Orotomide; inhibits fungal dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking pyrimidine synthesis. Oral development. Aspergillus, including some azole-resistant isolates, and selected difficult molds such as Scedosporium and Lomentospora. No useful Candida or Mucorales coverage. Investigational. OASIS phase 3 topline results were announced in June 2026; the October 6 sponsor statement still says it is unapproved. Full published results and regulatory review are needed to define its role. Fosmanogepix → manogepix Prodrug of a Gwt1 inhibitor affecting GPI-anchored protein maturation; IV and oral development. Broad investigational yeast and mold activity, including many resistant isolates. Important gaps include poor activity against C. krusei and related species; Mucorales activity is inconsistent. Small single-arm phase 2 studies reported clinical activity in candidemia and mold infections; comparative efficacy is not established. Two phase 3 programs for invasive yeast and mold infections were ongoing in the 2026 sponsor update. No established routine clinical TDM target or licensed regimen. Opelconazole Inhaled triazole designed for lung exposure. Local Aspergillus-directed development; inhalation does not establish adequate systemic or CNS therapy. Opera-T phase 3 in refractory pulmonary aspergillosis was terminated January 7, 2026. Sponsor interim analysis reported numerically worse response and higher mortality in the active arm. The unfavorable interim findings limit its proposed clinical role. [27] [28] [29] [30] [31] [32] [33] [34] Fellow teaching New mechanisms and resistance Olorofim is not an azole, and fosmanogepix is not an echinocandin. A new target may retain activity against isolates resistant to older classes. Spectrum, clinical efficacy, and emergence of resistance still require study. Assess the enrolled organisms, comparator, outcomes, follow-up, and safety data before applying trial results. [27] [32]

slides.title: Investigational antifungals
paragraphs: Fellow teaching
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Investigational antifungals Development status was reviewed October 14, 2026. These agents remain investigational; in vitro activity and sponsor announcements have limited clinical applicability. Agent Target / route Potential spectrum and gaps Current evidence and status Olorofim Orotomide; inhibits fungal dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking pyrimidine synthesis. Oral development. Aspergillus, including some azole-resistant isolates, and selected difficult molds such as Scedosporium and Lomentospora. No useful Candida or Mucorales coverage. Investigational. OASIS phase 3 topline results were announced in June 2026; the October 6 sponsor statement still says it is unapproved. Full published results and regulatory review are needed to define its role. Fosmanogepix → manogepix Prodrug of a Gwt1 inhibitor affecting GPI-anchored protein maturation; IV and oral development. Broad investigational yeast and mold activity, including many resistant isolates. Important gaps include poor activity against C. krusei and related species; Mucorales activity is inconsistent. Small single-arm phase 2 studies reported clinical activity in candidemia and mold infections; comparative efficacy is not established. Two phase 3 programs for invasive yeast and mold infections were ongoing in the 2026 sponsor update. No established routine clinical TDM target or licensed regimen. Opelconazole Inhaled triazole designed for lung exposure. Local Aspergillus-directed development; inhalation does not establish adequate systemic or CNS therapy. Opera-T phase 3 in refractory pulmonary aspergillosis was terminated January 7, 2026. Sponsor interim analysis reported numerically worse response and higher mortality in the active arm. The unfavorable interim findings limit its proposed clinical role. [27] [28] [29] [30] [31] [32] [33] [34] Fellow teaching New mechanisms and resistance Olorofim is not an azole, and fosmanogepix is not an echinocandin. A new target may retain activity against isolates resistant to older classes. Spectrum, clinical efficacy, and emergence of resistance still require study. Assess the enrolled organisms, comparator, outcomes, follow-up, and safety data before applying trial results. [27] [32]

slides.title: Rounds sheet
paragraphs: Identify the organism and infection site. Identify source control. Confirm formulation, load, organ function, interaction review, and the monitoring owner.
Fluconazole: no Aspergillus/Mucorales, but active against Cryptococcus and Coccidioides. Itraconazole: usual Histo/Blasto azole. Voriconazole: no Mucorales. Dematiaceous molds: species-dependent.
Itraconazole: negative inotropy/CHF. Voriconazole: visual/neuro effects, QT, photosensitivity, periostitis. Posaconazole: hypertension/hypokalemia. Isavuconazole: QT shortening.
slides.notes:
Complete source section:
Rounds sheet Before the first dose Identify the organism and infection site. Identify source control. Confirm formulation, load, organ function, interaction review, and the monitoring owner. Coverage gaps Fluconazole: no Aspergillus/Mucorales, but active against Cryptococcus and Coccidioides. Itraconazole: usual Histo/Blasto azole. Voriconazole: no Mucorales. Dematiaceous molds: species-dependent. Adverse effects Itraconazole: negative inotropy/CHF. Voriconazole: visual/neuro effects, QT, photosensitivity, periostitis. Posaconazole: hypertension/hypokalemia. Isavuconazole: QT shortening. Amphotericin plan Name the formulation. Follow creatinine, K, Mg, CBC, and liver tests. Plan replacement, infusion management, and appropriate hydration. TDM calculation Itraconazole + hydroxyitraconazole only when using a combined target. Do not add a metabolite to voriconazole. Document draw timing and assay. Site of infection CSF is not a brain tissue level. Candiduria often needs no antifungal. Micafungin has poor urine exposure; renal tissue infection from candidemia is different. See the linked sources and main tables for dosing and target qualifications.
